data.gender_notes: Shresth is used as a masculine name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is the best, the chief, the leader, the excellent one. The name Shresth carries the meaning “Excellent, Best, Chief” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shresth usually hope their child will grow to embody excellent, best, chief and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Shresth belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Excellent, Best, Chief.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shresth total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

This name is often attributed to individuals who have achieved great success, excellence, or have excelled in a particular field.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Shresth" symbolizes the pursuit of excellence and striving towards self-improvement and personal growth. It reminds us of the importance of constantly working towards being the best version of ourselves and upholding the values of truth, wisdom, and morality.

historical_references.reference: Shresth Prajapati was a legendary sage and a Rishi in Hindu mythology, considered as the elder brother of King Ikshvaku, the founder of the Solar Dynasty and the Ikshvaku lineage. He is said to have performed the Rajasuya Yajna for King Ikshvaku, bestowing him with supreme royal power and victories.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology and early Indian history

historical_references.reference: King Shresthakarma of the Lunar Dynasty, also known as the moon dynasty, is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the father of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty. He is renowned for his wisdom and is considered the architect of the great Kurukshetra battlefield where the famous Mahabharata war was fought.
historical_references.context: Hindu epic Mahabharata and ancient Indian history
